subject: MSA + Order Form: IP & productization language — proposed compromise
messages:
From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acmedata.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.inference>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmedata.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: MSA & Order Form — IP & Productization language

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement asked us to open a thread to nail down three specific items in the MSA/order form before we proceed to countersign:

1) Output ownership: Acme wants explicit language assigning ownership of AI-generated outputs to Acme for productization (we plan to embed generated copy into our platform widgets).
2) Training/data use: We need assurance that Redwood will not use Acme data or outputs to retrain models that could be sold or redistributed, unless we opt-in in writing.
3) Feedback/license: Any telemetry or feedback Redwood collects should be limited and anonymized; we want narrow rights so outputs aren't used beyond service improvements.

I attached our proposed redlines (acme_proposed_redlines.docx). Could you confirm Redwood's position and whether you'd be open to a limited productization carveout or a paid add-on to allow model retraining?

Procurement also asked for an estimated timeline for legal sign-off (they hope to close by end of next week).

Thanks,
Sophie Turner
Head of Partnerships, Acme DataWorks

Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — IP & Productization language

Sophie,

Appreciate the clear asks and the redlines. I looped in Laura (Legal) and Ben (Sales lead) so we can propose a compromise that balances Acme's productization needs and Redwood's product/eval protections.

High-level response:
- Output ownership: Redwood generally grants customers rights to use and display outputs in their products, but we cannot assign model IP or grant rights that enable redistribution of our models themselves. We can propose explicit language that grants Acme a perpetual, irrevocable right to use outputs in Acme products (including commercialization) while preserving Redwood's ownership of model weights and underlying training improvements.
- Training/data use: We are prepared to commit to a default "no retrain" posture (Redwood will not use customer-provided content or derived outputs to retrain models used in Redwood's public model catalog) unless Acme opts in to a separate training agreement or paid feature.
- Feedback license: We can agree to a limited, anonymized telemetry license for service improvements; if Acme needs telemetry to be excluded entirely, we'll document a paid telemetry-exclusion option.

Next steps I propose:
1) Laura, can you draft short clause options (two alternatives: conservative customer-favoring and balanced compromise) that we can send back to Acme?
2) Ben, please confirm whether we want to offer a paid "productization add-on" or keep it as a negotiation lever.
3) Sophie, I'll return with a compact tracked-change MSA + order form redline by Tuesday EOD.

Attached: redwood_response_redline.docx (high level comments)

Grace O'Connor

Grace, Ben —

I reviewed Acme's requested redlines and Grace's notes. Below are two short, legally precise options we can present. Both preserve Redwood's core IP while giving Acme productization rights to outputs.

Option A (Customer-favoring, narrow exceptions):
"Customer shall own all right, title and interest in and to Outputs generated solely from Customer Input. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood retains all rights in the Model(s), underlying weights, architectures, and any aggregated or de-identified telemetry. Redwood will not use Customer Input or Outputs to retrain or improve any public or commercial models without Customer's prior written opt-in. Where Customer wishes to enable model retraining, the parties will enter a separate training agreement and associated fee schedule."

Option B (Balanced compromise — recommended):
"Customer is granted a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free right to use, reproduce, and display Outputs in Customer's products and services. Redwood retains ownership of Models, weights, and derivative model IP. Redwood may collect anonymized usage telemetry for service improvements and model quality monitoring, provided such telemetry does not include Customer Input or Output in identifiable form. Redwood will not use Customer Input or Output to retrain models used to serve other customers except where Customer has provided express written consent or entered a separately negotiated training arrangement. Any productization rights that would permit redistribution of Redwood's model artifacts are expressly excluded."

Practical notes:
- Option B avoids an absolute ban on any use of de-identified telemetry (reduces operational friction) while preserving a clear opt-in path for retraining.
- If Acme insists on an assignment of Output IP, we should ask for a commercial offset (e.g., higher subscription fee or a one-time IP assignment fee) since that materially affects product roadmap and potential model monetization.

I attached a short text file with the clause language ready for track changes. Happy to edit further for negotiation tone.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — IP & Productization language

Sophie / Acme team —

Following internal review, please find attached a compact proposed redline that implements the compromise language our counsel recommended (see attached orderform_redline_trackchanges.pdf). High-level summary:

- Outputs: Redwood grants Acme a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive right to use and commercialize Outputs in Acme's products. This covers embedding generated content in product UI, downstream resale of the product, and derivative works created from Outputs.
- Model IP: Redwood retains ownership of model weights, code, and any model artifacts; assignment of model IP is not on the table.
- Training: Default is no retraining with Customer Input/Outputs. If Acme wants Redwood to use datasets derived from Acme for retraining, we'll require a separate training addendum and fee.
- Feedback/Telemetry: Redwood will collect only anonymized telemetry for reliability and quality improvements; we propose a telemetry-exclusion paid option if Acme requires no telemetry collection.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
1) Acme to review the attached redline and confirm acceptance or provide targeted counters.
2) If Acme requests assignment language, please flag so we can prepare commercial terms.
3) We aim to finalize legal language by EOD Friday to keep the deal on track.

Link: Mutual Action Plan (MAP): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3cMAP-acme-redline

Attachments: orderform_redline_trackchanges.pdf

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call if that helps speed alignment.

Best,
